To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The memory footprint and power consumption are the main bottlenecks in CNNs on constrained platforms, and 2) The number of convolution layers, the size of filters, subsampling technique, and the number of fully-connected layers have a considerable impact in the overall performance.
we show how the design and implementation of CNNs can be tailored for constrained environments by modifying specific network design properties.

we have analyzed the memory and computational complexity of each layer in a CNN, and have optimized the design parameters to achieve the highest accuracy with the lowest power and memory footprint on an FPGA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: (i) analyzing the impact of network design on performance and efficiency; and (ii) developing a systematic approach to optimizing and implementing networks on constrained platforms.
the efficient implementation of Convolutional Neural networks on resource constrained platforms and we demonstrate a systematic approach to achieve this goal.
understanding the trade-offs of different network design parameters, and their effect on memory and compute efficiency on constrained platforms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we can obtain the state of the art accuracy for MNIST and CIF AR 10 classification tasks using a relatively small network with 1,000 filters.
the design and implementation of CNNs is not only an art but also a science.
the design and optimization of neural networks is an art, and not a science, as it is highly dependent on the application and target platform.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of CNNs is a trade-off between accuracy, memory footprint, power, and performance, and we show how to make informed decisions for a given target accuracy.

we provide an insight on the impact of each layer of the CNN on memory footprint, latency, and power consumption and how to modify the network to achieve a better performance on constrained platforms.

by breaking down CNNs into layers and analyzing their impact on performance, we enable informed design choices and optimizations that are crucial for efficient implementations on constrained platforms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a careful design of the CNN architecture and its implementation is essential in achieving a power efficient and low latency inference on low power computing platforms.

a deep understanding of the CNN architecture, and the ability to optimize the network for specific constraints, can enable significant improvements in energy efficiency, and thus, enable new applications.
a careful analysis of the design of CNNs can lead to significant gains in efficiency, and can enable the implementation of these networks on constrained platforms.
